title: Timeline Glitch
blurb: History's calendar is glitching. Three of these really line up. One is pure cap.

cards.say: [Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid], [the tin can was invented more than 40 years before the can opener], [the Inca Empire was still standing when the Mayflower sailed to America], and [Shakespeare was still alive when the English founded Jamestown].
cards.real: Spain conquered the Inca in the 1530s, and their last stronghold fell in 1572, nearly 50 years before the Mayflower sailed in 1620.

cards.say: [the supersonic Concorde made its last passenger flight in 1993], [Western Union sent its very last telegram in 2006], [the US government was still paying a Civil War pension in 2020], and [a Japanese temple-building company stayed independent for over 1,400 years].
cards.real: The Concorde's last passenger flights were in 2003, when Air France and British Airways retired it after 27 years of service.

cards.say: [two pilots flew nonstop across the Atlantic before Charles Lindbergh did], [Orville Wright lived to see a plane fly faster than sound], [hot-air balloons carried people before the US Constitution was signed], and [the first parachute jump came after the first airplane flight].
cards.real: People parachuted long before airplanes: André-Jacques Garnerin jumped from a balloon over Paris in 1797, over 100 years before the Wright brothers flew.

cards.say: [teaching at Oxford began before the Aztecs founded their capital, Tenochtitlan], [the Washington Monument was finished before the US Civil War began], [London's Underground trains were running during the US Civil War], and [the game of basketball is older than the teddy bear].
cards.real: Work began in 1848 but stopped in 1854 when the money ran out. It restarted in 1880, and the monument was finished in 1884, long after the war.

cards.say: [Charles Schulz died the night before his last Peanuts comic strip ran], [Isaac Newton was born on the very day that Galileo died], [Thomas Jefferson and John Adams died on the very same day], and [Mark Twain was born and died in years when Halley's Comet flew by].
cards.real: Galileo died in January 1642. Newton was born almost a year later, on Christmas Day 1642 by England's calendar back then. The same-day story is a myth.

cards.say: [Pac-Man hit arcades before the first music CDs went on sale], [Nintendo's Game Boy came out the same year the Berlin Wall fell], [the first Toy Story movie came out before Google was founded], and [Netflix was streaming movies online before YouTube existed].
cards.real: YouTube launched in 2005. Netflix mailed out DVDs for years and didn't start streaming movies until 2007.

cards.say: [the Golden Gate Bridge took 14 years to build], [Louis XIV was king of France for 72 years], [the Empire State Building was built in just 410 days], and [the Hundred Years' War actually lasted 116 years].
cards.real: Building the Golden Gate Bridge took just over four years: work began in January 1933, and it opened in May 1937.

cards.say: [the fax machine was patented before the telephone], [a submarine powered by oars traveled along London's River Thames in the 1620s], [the first photograph was taken after the telephone was invented], and [an engineer in ancient Alexandria built a coin-operated vending machine].
cards.real: The oldest surviving photo was taken in France around 1826, about 50 years before Bell patented the telephone in 1876.

cards.say: [the Soviets sent a woman to space 20 years before the US did], [people walked on the Moon within 66 years of the first airplane flight], [astronauts walked on the Moon before the first home video game console was sold], and [the first person to float outside a spacecraft was an American].
cards.real: Soviet cosmonaut Alexei Leonov made the first spacewalk in March 1965. American Ed White made his less than three months later.

cards.say: [Pepsi was invented before Coca-Cola went on sale], [Oreo cookies were around before Mickey Mouse was created], [Jell-O was invented before the Wright brothers first flew], and [jigsaw puzzles are older than the United States].
cards.real: Coca-Cola first went on sale in 1886. Pepsi came along in the 1890s as Brad's Drink, and only got the name Pepsi-Cola in 1898.

cards.say: [Leonardo da Vinci started the Mona Lisa after Columbus reached the Americas], [Genghis Khan was still alive when England's Magna Carta was sealed], [Joan of Arc was still alive when Gutenberg printed his famous Bible], and [Isaac Newton and Benjamin Franklin were alive at the same time].
cards.real: Joan of Arc died in 1431. Gutenberg printed his famous Bible in the mid-1450s, more than 20 years later.
src: NOT WEB-CHECKED (textbook) Joan of Arc died in May 1431; Gutenberg's 42-line Bible was printed around 1454-1455

cards.say: [people could pay for video phone calls before the Moon landing], [the first text message was sent before the first website went online], [Kodak built the first digital camera before the first Star Wars movie came out], and [the computer mouse is older than the Super Bowl].
cards.real: The first website went online at CERN at the end of 1990. The first text message wasn't sent until December 1992.
